body:
Fixes [LINK_REMOVED].

Two gaps in the fixed-point / Decimal types:

**1. `{:F}` (Decimal) could not parse a negative number.** `"F"` was missing from the `is_numeric` set, so it never got the shared `[-+ ]?` sign prefix every other numeric type receives:

```python
>>> parse.parse("{:F}", "-2.5")   # None on master
>>> parse.parse("{:f}", "-2.5")   # -2.5 (float, same regex, works)
```

Broken since `F` was added ([LINK_REMOVED]); the general signed-number fix ([LINK_REMOVED]) added the prefix but never listed `F`. One character: `"n%fegdobxEGX"` -> `"n%fFegdobxEGX"`.

**2. `{:f}`/`{:F}` did not parse `nan`/`inf`,** although `{:e}`/`{:E}`/`{:g}`/`{:G}` already do and `"{:f}".format(float("nan")) == "nan"`. The `nan|NAN|inf|INF` alternation is added inside a non-capturing group so the leading `[-+ ]?` stays in front of the whole alternation; a bare append would bind the sign to the first branch only and break negative parsing (that is the subtlety here, and why `f`/`F` need grouping where `e`/`g` did not).

Tests: added Decimal-sign and `f`/`F` nan/inf cases to `test_numbers` (they fail on `master`), and updated `test_numbered`, which pins the exact `{:f}` regex string. Full suite: 97 passed, 1 skipped.
